items.title: datasette-leaflet 0.3
items.summary: Release: datasette-leaflet 0.3 OpenStreetMap have a very reasonable policy that hits to their hosted tile server should send a referrer header . Datasette table pages used the Referrer-Policy: no-referrer HTTP header, causing plugins that loaded tiles from OpenStreetMap to violate that policy. datasette-leaflet is the plugin that loads a bundled Leaflet so other Datasette plugins can depend on it. It now sets the referrer policy on the tile requests themselves to strict-origin-when-cross-origin , passing the host but not the full path to the page. Tags: leaflet , datasette , openstreetmap

items.title: What if you dove into the Sun?
items.summary: What if you dove into the Sun? The photosphere is about 5,500 Celsius and about 400 kilometers thick, hotter than the roughly 3,640 Celsius where carbon turns to gas. The convection zone below it reaches up to 2 million degrees, light can take up to 170,000 years to cross the radiative zone, and the core tops 15 million degrees. Idea: Cleo Abram. Sources: NASA Sun facts and the NASA Marshall solar interior page. Footage: NASA SDO, Storyblocks. Depth and temperature between the NASA figures are approximate. Which layer would stop you first? Sources, in order of the dive: Photosphere about 5,500 C (10,000 F), about 250 miles (400 km) thick; the convection zone drops below 2 million C; about 170,000 years from the core to the top of the convection zone; the core tops 15 million C; hydrogen is fused into helium: NASA, science.nasa.gov/sun/facts Convection zone from about 200,000 km deep to the surface, 2,000,000 C at its base; radiative zone from 25 percent to 70 percent of the way to the surface; core 175,000 km from the centre: NASA Marshall, solarscience.msfc.nasa.gov/interior.shtml The depth and temperature counter moves between those NASA numbers, so the digits in between are appr...

items.title: What happens if you don't put your phone in airplane mode?
items.summary: What happens on a flight if you don't put your phone in airplane mode? In the US, 5G phones use 3.7 to 3.98 GHz and the radar altimeter that measures height above the ground works at 4.2 to 4.4 GHz, a gap of 220 MHz. In Europe the phone band is 3.4 to 3.8 GHz, a gap of 400 MHz. EASA leaves it to each airline to decide whether devices can stay on. Idea: Mark Rober, his Short "What happens if you don't use Airplane mode?". Sources: FAA radio altimeter rule and the FCC Upper C-band order (Federal Register, July 31, 2026), EU Decision 2019/235, EASA. The 3D scene is a diagram, not to scale. Sound effects: Storyblocks. Airplane mode on every flight? Yes or no. Sources (the video shows the US and European gaps; the FCC step is written context only): Radar altimeter band 4.2-4.4 GHz, US 5G Lower C-band 3.70-3.98 GHz, Upper C-band 3.98-4.2 GHz, and the FAA's wording that an altimeter under interference can give "inaccurate altitude information": FAA final rule "Requirements for Interference-Tolerant Radio Altimeter Systems" (Federal Register, July 31, 2026): https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/31/2026-15585/requirements-for-interference-tolerant-radio-altimeter-systems FCC or...

items.title: llm 0.37.2
items.summary: Release: llm 0.37.2 Fixes a security issue reported by Daniel de Araujo in GHSA-v9h7-jj4g-f862 and GHSA-r639-rr7r-x72w . LLM has a mechanism called extra-openai-models.yaml - now managed by the new-in-0.37 llm openai endpoint add command - for using LLM with OpenAI-compatible API endpoints from other providers. Daniel reported two ways this could accidentally send your configured OpenAI API key to one of those providers: if the key named by api_key_name had never been stored, or if a responses: true model was run with -o chat_completions 1 . Tags: projects , security , llm , releases

items.title: How Model ML Is Building the AI Operating System For Finance
items.summary: Model ML (W24) is building the AI operating system for financial services, used by the largest banks, asset managers, and consulting firms in the world. Eighteen months after coming out of stealth, they’ve gone from 10 people to 200 across eight offices, and they’re still adding about 20 a week. At YC x London, co-founder and CEO Chaz Englander sat down with YC’s Gustaf Alströmer to talk about why agent harnesses couldn’t work with Excel until February, how to get investors to tell you the truth about why they passed, and why he thinks every founder in Europe is being insufficiently ambitious. items.title: A New Vision for Human Work After Automation
items.summary: Thesis: 2027 is made possible by our founding partners, Lovable and Notion. Lovable is the fastest way to turn ideas into software people love: https://link.lovable.dev/every Notion is the collaborative AI workspace where teams and agents work side by side: https://www.notion.com/?utm_source=youtube&utm_campaign=thesis-2027&utm_content=every-261111-video What does great human work look like after automation? It’s a question we try to answer every day at Every, and the one we built our conference, Thesis, around. In his closing keynote, *Dan Shipper* argues that as AI makes intelligence cheap and widely available, what matters most is human perspective. It’s your “non-consensus” point of view, plus your responsibility for a particular corner of the world, that helps you spot the insight no one else would. On this week’s episode of The Every Podcast, we’re sharing Dan’s full talk at Thesis: 2027. Dan explains why benchmark charts make the future of work look bleaker than it is, why picking the right idea still takes a human, and how we should really measure AI models.
